summary: Spaizone Vitals is a health monitoring dashboard that helps astronauts on long missions spot health changes early, without waiting for Earth. It learns each astronaut’s own normal baseline, uses rules and a machine learning anomaly model to flag drift in heart rate, oxygen, sleep, temperature, mood and radiation, and tells the astronaut what to do next.
details:
Problem. On missions to the Moon and Mars, astronauts face radiation, microgravity, isolation and stress. These cause slow changes such as bone loss, cardiovascular strain, immune changes and mental health decline. Communication delays mean astronauts must often notice these changes themselves.

Solution. Spaizone Vitals is a health monitoring dashboard that runs on board and needs no connection to Earth. It tracks six indicators every day: resting heart rate, blood oxygen, sleep, core temperature, mood check-ins and radiation dose rate.

How it works.

  1. Personal baseline. Each astronaut’s first 14 days set their own normal, because healthy ranges differ between people.
  2. Drift detection. A 5-day rolling average smooths daily noise. A move of 2σ in the unwanted direction raises a Watch, and 3σ raises an Alert. Radiation is also checked against a 250 mSv 30-day limit.
  3. Anomaly model. A k-nearest-neighbour model learns the astronaut’s normal combination of all six readings from the first 30 days. It scores how far each new day is from that normal. It catches several small shifts that happen together, even when no single reading has crossed its own limit.
  4. Guidance. Each warning comes with plain actions, such as a heart check, protecting sleep, calling behavioral health, or moving to shielded areas during a solar event.
  5. Ground report. A summary for the ground medical team is generated automatically on board.

Data input. Users can upload or paste a CSV, or add one day at a time, so the same dashboard works with real sensor data.

Benefits. It is personalized, catches slow changes early, supports crew autonomy during communication delays, and works offline.

Tools. HTML, CSS and JavaScript. All analysis runs in the browser.
